rows.item: A dispute's evidence reads the live board.

After a reload (or in another tab) a joiner whose link is older than 24 h but whose wallet proof was renewed since still reads "Re-prove <wallet> to deposit" (Deposit offered beside it): the RoomView shows only when the link was made, not when its proof was last verified.
rows.src: CONFIRMED (source, `19c021c`) — the proof time is stored and omitted: every proven grant carries `proof.verified_at` (`server/src/escrow/walletTickets.ts`:127; `renewProof` writes the new proof, keeps `issued_at`; persisted whole by `walletTicketFileStore.ts`:74-83 and `aws/game/dynamoTicketStore.ts`); the admission judges it (`escrowPorts.ts`:395 `WALLET_PROOF_MAX_AGE_MS`, 416); the projection sends `linkedAt: link.issued_at` only (`moneyTables.ts`:935; `standingLinkOf` :377-380 guarantees `proof !== null`); the browser infers from `linkedAt` plus this page's own record (`money/useMoneyTable.ts` `proof`, `money/moneySession.ts` `proofRenewedAt`, never persisted).
rows.slice: W2-M (server addition owner-authorized 2026-10-04 for exactly this row; the browser-only boundary otherwise stands)
rows.notes: Implemented as the smallest additive change: `you.link.proofVerifiedAt` = the standing grant's stored `proof.verified_at` (`moneyTables.ts` projection); no migration, contract, codec, ledger-format, FINANCIAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION or hosted-protocol change (an additive server-to-client field). The browser takes the newest of it and this page's own accepted re-proof: past 24 h by that time it is the server's word (Re-prove, no Deposit beside it); inside the 5-minute margin, or with the field absent or malformed (an older server), the page's inference (Re-prove with Deposit beside it). Residual (LOW, accepted): the age is judged on this device's clock; a clock hours ahead still reads a fresh proof as stale -- one free re-proof, never a deposit taken. OWNER DESIGN DIRECTION (2026-10-04): the Profile + Keplr flow is PROVISIONAL and slated for a later redesign/rebuild; this row is a minimal, removable compatibility change, not an endorsement of the current flow (no new UI surface, no new authority). **W3-L (2026-10-05):** the Profile + Keplr redesign this direction anticipated is W3-L (P3-ACCT, `phase3/preplaytest-profile-account-wallet` `9afc74a`, NOT integrated); this row's behaviour (authoritative `proofVerifiedAt`, pre-sign replacement disclosure, single-use challenge, replay protection) is kept unchanged under it and was re-reviewed.
rows.status: IMPLEMENTED — W2-M `a97b1d1` + review fix `9637ca7`, INTEGRATED on `phase3/consolidated-pre-playtest-integration` (2026-10-05): the room view carries the stored proof time; freshness after a reload follows it

rows.item: When the page does not yet show the seat's standing link (a stale view: another tab or device linked a wallet moments before), Link / Re-prove is answered `replace-required` after Keplr signed, and confirming the replacement needs a second Keplr signature.
rows.src: CONFIRMED (source, `19c021c`) — `moneyTables.ts` `walletLink`: `challenges.take` -> ADR-036 verify -> actor `linkDecision` (`replace-required` 409 when the newest standing proven grant is another wallet and `replace` is absent, :1288-1291) -> `finish()` spends the nonce on every non-503 answer with that answer cached (:1319-1322); `walletProof.ts` `ChallengeBook.spend` / `take` (a retry of the same signature returns the cached 409; a new signature on a spent nonce is `challenge-used`). The challenge text binds site, network, contract, game, seat, wallet, nonce and expiry -- not the replace intent -- so only a new mint + signature can carry `replace: true`. W2-M (AUD-20.03) already asks first whenever the VIEW shows the link; only the stale-view race is left.
rows.slice: W2-M (server addition owner-authorized 2026-10-04 for exactly this row; the browser-only boundary otherwise stands)
rows.notes: Implemented as approved (the safer design): `wallet-challenge` also answers `replaces` -- the seat's standing linked wallet when it is another wallet (null: nothing replaced; omitted if the ledger can't be read). The browser asks before Keplr signs (the unspent challenge is superseded by the next mint), then signs once with `replace: true`; a confirmed replacement refuses before signing if the wallet the fresh challenge names is not the one shown (or, from an older server, the view's), and a question raised by the server's own post-signature `replace-required` asks again about the wallet the fresh challenge names. Unchanged: the challenge's single use, the cached answer for a retry, `challenge-used`, `challenge-expired`, the link's own decision and refusal order; the alternative (reusing a consumed challenge / retrying the same signed request) is NOT implemented. Residual (LOW, owner's call, not approved scope): the check is before signing only -- a link made by another device of the same principal while Keplr's prompt is open is still replaced by the plain `replace: true` (as before W2-M); closing it would need an additive `replaceWallet` on wallet-link. OWNER DESIGN DIRECTION (2026-10-04): the Profile + Keplr flow is PROVISIONAL and slated for a later redesign/rebuild; this row is a minimal, removable compatibility change, not an endorsement of the current flow (no new UI surface, no new authority). **W3-L (2026-10-05):** the Profile + Keplr redesign this direction anticipated is W3-L (P3-ACCT, `phase3/preplaytest-profile-account-wallet` `9afc74a`, NOT integrated); this row's behaviour (authoritative `proofVerifiedAt`, pre-sign replacement disclosure, single-use challenge, replay protection) is kept unchanged under it and was re-reviewed.

rows.item: Owner-observed (2026-10-04): a seated principal pressed the Lobby's public-list "Watch" on their own game; the table opened in their SEAT, ONE TURN BEHIND the game, and offered them their turn from that stale board. Three separate facts: (a) WATCH IDENTITY -- Watch and "Your tables" are one door (`onEnterSandbox(gameId)`); no watch intent reaches the shell or the wire, and the seat is the server's principal -> seat answer, so a participant who presses Watch is seated, against the button's "You will not have a seat."; (b) STALE AT REST -- the drain counts an entry applied before dispatching it, with no catch and no retry, and on a fresh entry the first board comparison is muted (console only), so the board can rest behind the room with no notice; (c) ACTIONABLE WHILE STALE -- the only currentness gate is a drain in progress; the turn gate reads the shell's own board, and the link stamps a click with the index it RECEIVED, so the server's staleness guard does not fire and the click is judged on the real board (refused, or APPLIED when legal there).
rows.src: CONFIRMED (source + in-memory tests, `phase3W3GWatchDefect.test.tsx`) — (a) `Lobby.tsx` `onWatch` / `onOpen` -> `onEnterSandbox`; `App.tsx` `handleEnterSandbox` (no intent, `mode: "sandbox"`); `server/src/rooms/gameRecord.ts` `roomViewFor` role by `seatOf(record, principalId)`; `LobbyRoomList.tsx` Watch title. (b) `App.tsx` drain `appliedCountRef.current = at + 1` before `await runGameplayActionRef.current?.(...)`, try/finally only; `divergenceWatch.ts` `everAgreed` false -> `message: null`. The exact trigger of the owner's stale entry (a client reducer no-op / refusal vs a thrown replay) is NOT PROVEN -- the owner's console (`[divergence] … have not agreed` vs an unhandled rejection) distinguishes them. (c) `App.tsx` turn gate (`replayingRef` only; `actingAddress(boardNow, …)`); `serverLink.ts` `flushUnsent` `baseIndex: appliedIndex` advanced in `applyEntries`; `roomSession.ts` staleness `baseIndex < nextIndex - 1` -- a tip-stamped click from a stale board is refused by authority, or applied (test: index 3 lands).
rows.notes: HIGH (owner-accepted 2026-10-04): a stale view can submit, the click reaches the server and can land (proven in memory; no live game touched). (A) OD-19 RULED: Watch always opens a READ-ONLY spectator view, even for a principal who holds a seat; it never silently reinterprets the viewer as their seated player; re-entering an owned seat is the participant path ("Your tables" / Open / Rejoin); the control keeps "Watch this game. You will not have a seat." (B), (C) OPEN / W3-J under the stale-board safety requirement (status). Characterization tests `components/phase3W3GWatchDefect.test.tsx` stay as triage evidence: DEFECT tests flip in W3-J, KEEP tests (the Play / Rejoin seat path) stay.
rows.status: IMPLEMENTED — W3-J under OD-19 (triage `d3f9050` and ruling `3be965d` merged by `d4a4ca1`): (A) READ-ONLY WATCH -- `fd3bbda` (the Lobby's Watch is its own door, `activeGame.watch` persisted; `utils/watchView.ts` projects the room view as a watcher's: no seat, no host, no Start) + review fixes `e538039` (a Watch tab gives up no seat, offers no Take a seat, sends no room op) and `45272e6` (a Watch tab's Leave returns to the Lobby); (B) NOT SILENTLY BEHIND -- `utils/boardCurrency.ts` + RED R5 `7c4624f` (a drain pass that throws latches the board as not current) and the settle point's standing digest mismatch: isMyTurn false and a forced native-modal BoardBehindNotice (Reload / Back to the lobby); (C) NOT ACTIONABLE -- RED R1 `b4c1714` (the send gate refuses a board that is not current, or a Watch tab, before the turn gate) and RED R5 `8c5ff63` (each submission bound to the position the board APPLIED; the server's existing anchored staleness guard answers a behind board with a catch-up, nothing applied). No server, wire or engine change. The characterization DEFECT tests flipped, KEEP tests (the participant seat path) stay. Tests `components/phase3W3JWatchStaleBoard.test.tsx` (end to end through the real link and the real RoomSession: a move chosen on a board resting behind the room settles `null` and does not land), `utils/phase3W3JRed.test.ts`. Recorded residual (LOW, review): a latch whose cause recurs on every load keeps that table blocked until fixed -- OD-19's fail-safe, accepting #1223's false-positive cost. Not integrated. INTEGRATED on `phase3/consolidated-pre-playtest-integration` (2026-10-05). OD-19 (owner, 2026-10-05): the RED R1 / R5 lines that carry the stale-board requirement (`b4c1714`, `7c4624f`, `8c5ff63`) are NOT re-asked for owner confirmation; the fail-closed behaviour when a board cannot converge (a not-current latch blocks the table until reload) is an intentional safety property and is preserved.

rows.item: A player deciding whether to join a stranger's money table has no factual history to read. Wanted: facts, never a composite score -- member since / account age, completed money games, distinct ESTABLISHED profiles played with, unresolved disputes, verified-wallet status, dispute / forfeit history -- under "Profile history", "Prior relationships", "Identity assurance".
rows.src: CONFIRMED (`b8d5246`): no trust surface. The durable records already hold what is needed: the profile's creation time and wallet (identity), each GameRecord's seats / money / `completed_at`, the financial record's phase and chain outcome route.
rows.notes: NO canonical definition of an "established" profile exists in the repository or its history (searched: source, docs, the accounting JSON, the Project reports): none is invented. The data path (`opponentsOf` + the `ESTABLISHED_PROFILE` predicate slot, `server/src/rooms/trustFacts.ts`) fills that one fact once the owner defines it. Not sanctions, bans or a collusion score; the facts prove nothing about who controls a profile. OWNER RULING (2026-10-05, the account-policy follow-up): a profile is ESTABLISHED once it has COMPLETED at least one real-money game (cancelled, annulled and free games never count; no account-age requirement; no inference of common ownership from IP / device data).

rows.ids: owner rulings (final account / Authorization Wallet model)
rows.item: The owner's final model: THE PROFILE / ACCOUNT IS THE PLAYER; a Keplr wallet is not. An account is a username, a password (12+, no composition rules) and exactly ONE designated Authorization Wallet proven at creation by an ADR-036 signature over a fresh, short-lived, single-use, domain-separated server text (no transaction, no funds, no spend permission). Normal login is the username and password only. "Forgot password?" is the Authorization Wallet's (a one-time RECOVER signature; every session and family revoked; seats, trust, payout bindings and escrow ownership untouched; no enumeration oracle; gameplay wallets cannot recover). Changing it needs a signed-in, explicitly confirmed session plus the CURRENT wallet's approval and the NEW wallet's acceptance. The recovery-key product is removed entirely; no email; no operator override (lost password + lost wallet = no automated recovery); legacy profiles are disposable (retired, no migration).
rows.src: CONFIRMED (`caad745`): accounts were username + password + a recovery key (`rk_`), with key reset / rotation / re-authentication and link codes; the profile held a "verified payout wallet" persisted from the last wallet linked at any seat; no Authorization Wallet existed.
rows.notes: OWNER RULINGS 2026-10-06 (the final account / wallet identity brief). The internal credential epoch (recovery_selector + the sealed digest) is kept as an internal value -- no financial protocol bump, no certified signed format changed. No mainnet exceptional account-recovery authority exists.

rows.ids: owner rulings (all player games are anted; payout binding fixed once anted)
rows.item: Every player game is an anted game: no free player mode (no free create, join or start in the product; internal fixtures kept; no fake ante; escrow economics unchanged). Once a seat has anted, that game + seat's deposit / payout wallet is fixed: no relink to another wallet, account action or security event changes it; refunds and payouts are never redirected. Multi-game: Game 1 on Wallet A, Game 2 on Wallet B, Authorization Wallet C, ordinary play with no Keplr switching.

rows.item: A seated player has no way to report legal-but-harmful conduct (deliberate stalling / timing abuse, abusive trade-offer spam, harassment, suspected collusion, other) for operator review, and the operator has no preserved, server-derived evidence or small review workflow. Wanted: report from the table only (never anonymous), neutral categories, a short optional note, evidence preserved by the server (never screenshots, never credentials / session ids / IPs / devices / wallet-proof material), durable cases with statuses Open / Under review / No violation / Conduct issue confirmed / Escalated, a minimal reviewer panel; a report never punishes, changes a game, money, escrow or a profile, and never feeds a score or a public count.
rows.src: CONFIRMED (`caad745`): no report path, no conduct store, no review route or panel existed.
rows.notes: Reporting is conduct REVIEW and evidence preservation, not the first line of defence (the clock / trade lane owns the mechanical two-decline rule). Nothing infers motive from offer values: offers are COUNTED and TIMED, never judged. No trust score; nothing about reports is public; trust facts never read a case.

OD-4.title: EMERGENCY FUNDING (AUTOMATIC BANKRUPTCY)
ruling: Emergency funding becomes automatic in the v13 rules batch (owner sub-rulings O-1 to O-6 of V13_SCOPE_VERIFICATION §3.6).
O-1: the intercorporate trade window is budgeted at the treasury plus the president's cash before any liquidation; a ForgoTrainTrade message closes it; it never reopens.
O-3: a liquidation-funded intercorporate trade is illegal.
The treasury-plus-cash commitment and the purchase are automatic, through the derived-action machinery with durable keys.

Share raising is one atomic EmergencySellPortfolio: the submitted order is preserved; the whole portfolio is validated, simulated and proven legal; any failure returns the original board; ordinary sale law is reused.
O-4: "only enough" applies to the whole portfolio, and the smallest legal overshoot is allowed.
O-5: no self-created bankruptcy: an insufficient portfolio is refused. The insolvency oracle must be exact.
O-2: private funding stays optional; fundingPrivateOfferRefusal is preserved and ForgoPrivateFunding is added.

Bankruptcy is automatic, with no player Declare: liquidate as far as legally possible, apply the cash to the obligated corporation, then GameEnd with bankrupt_president. DeclareBankruptcy is refused on v13.
O-6: shares that could not be sold are scored as the bankrupt's shares.
Expose the authority W2-G needs. Not in this batch: DH-1, GR-1 / S10-27, GR-1b, D-18, D-22, RR-4, V-6.3.

Owner ruling 1 (2026-10-04): KEEP the portfolio rule. "Only enough" means no redundant leg and no unnecessarily large percentage within a leg when a smaller LEGAL bundle of that same holding would still fund; the smallest legal indivisible bundle may overshoot. It does NOT mean the globally smallest dollar overshoot: with $50 short, { B 10% } raising $100 and { C 10% } raising $60 are both legal and the player chooses.
Owner ruling 4 (2026-10-04): KEEP the refusal. EmergencySellPortfolio may contain each corporation at most once; 20% of PRR is one 20% leg, never two 10% legs.

Owner ruling 5 (2026-10-04): private-funding relevance is EXACT. The question is whether at least one legally valid private-funding path (one sale or a legal sequence, assuming buyer consent, under the existing #1541 authority) could contribute to a complete rescue. An upper bound may be used only to prune; if exact authority proves no legal private path can rescue, bankruptcy does not wait.

Review findings fixed (2026-10-04): the automatic bankruptcy is narrated as an outcome; the no-server shell forwards the keyed automatic emergency purchase through #1247's derived-action path; the Rules Reference trade-window and bankruptcy-warning copy; the v13 changelog wording.

OD-19.title: WATCH IS A READ-ONLY SPECTATOR VIEW (AUD-25.16)
ruling: ACCEPT the Watch defect classification as HIGH.
"Watch" always opens a READ-ONLY spectator view.
This remains true even when the signed-in user already occupies a seat in that game.
Watch must NOT silently reinterpret the viewer as their seated player.
Re-entering an owned seat belongs to the existing participant path: "Your tables" / Open / Rejoin.
Preserve the existing user-facing meaning already stated by the Watch control: "Watch this game. You will not have a seat."

Separately (AUD-25.16, independent of spectator policy): a client whose locally APPLIED board state is behind the authoritative game state must never be allowed to submit a gameplay action as though its board were current. The W3-J remediation addresses both layers -- CLIENT: while replay / catch-up / divergence remains unresolved, gameplay controls are non-actionable, and stale local turn authority must not enable a move; SUBMISSION / SERVER: do not rely only on the browser hiding / disabling controls; the submission must carry / bind to the revision / log position actually APPLIED to the client's board, not merely the newest log position received; the server must reject a gameplay action whose client-applied position does not match the authoritative pre-action position. The exact protocol implementation belongs to W3-J investigation / review.
OD-19.effect: OD-19: RULED. AUD-25.16 IMPLEMENTED by W3-J and INTEGRATED on `phase3/consolidated-pre-playtest-integration`: Watch is its own door and always a read-only spectator view (a seated principal included; the seat is reopened by Your tables / Open / Rejoin); CLIENT -- a board that is replaying, catching up or diverged is not current and nothing on it is actionable; SUBMISSION -- every submission is bound to the APPLIED board position; SERVER -- the existing anchored staleness guard rejects a position that is not the authoritative pre-action position. The owner does NOT re-ask confirmation of W3-J's RED edits (2026-10-05). The fail-closed behaviour when the board cannot converge is an intentional safety property and is preserved.

owner_decisions_open: Password minimum length: PROVISIONAL 8 characters (NIST SP 800-63B's floor for user-chosen secrets), maximum 1024 bytes; confirm or set (cleanPassword / PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH).

Username syntax: only the mechanism's bounds (NFKC, 1-64 code points with its canonical key, no control / format / unassigned characters, case-insensitive uniqueness by lower-casing). No reserved names, no character-class policy, no confusable / blank-glyph rule -- the owner's choice.
"Established" profile / opponent: no canonical definition exists; the count stays null until the owner defines it (ESTABLISHED_PROFILE in trustFacts.ts).

Password change / reset (security review M4, N-2): none is built (no email, by the brief). A leaked password has no player remedy short of an operator; a stolen LEGACY recovery key can set a password the owner then cannot replace (before this slice a stolen key could already rotate the key and lock the owner out). Proposal: a sensitive "change password" (current password or legacy key) that advances the credential epoch and signs out the other devices.

Lockout trade-offs: wrong-password budgets per address (200 + 600/h), per username and address (10 + 20/h), per username overall (50 + 100/h backstop, which a distributed guesser can keep spent), reauth per device family (10 + 20/h) and per account (20 + 20/h); "username taken" on create reveals that a username exists (bounded by the create budgets).
KDF parameters (scrypt N=2^15, r=8, p=3) and the gate (4 at once, 2 per address, one slot reserved for signed-in confirmations; UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE 16) against the production host's CPU.

Visitor scope: public tables' chat and watcher slots are now reachable by signed-out visitors (OD-19 read-only); visitor sockets per browser stay capped at 6 (maxSocketsPerProvisionalPrincipal) and visitors count against a table's watcher cap.

w3l_account_policy_followup.recovery_model: The key is the LIVE-2E key (128-bit selector + 256-bit secret; stored as the selector and SHA-256 of the secret). It never goes to a URL, log, storage, game record or chain; it appears only in the create and rotation answers (no-store). On an account WITH a password it only replaces credentials: "Forgot password?" (reset), the reauth credential of "Change password", and its own replacement -- /gs/api/profile/recover answers 409 use-password-reset (only to a valid key's holder) and "Confirm it's you" refuses it. A profile with NO password (legacy) still signs in with it and sets a username + password under a key-confirmed grant; afterwards its key is recovery only. One key at a time (selector CAS). Rotation needs an EXPLICIT "Confirm it's you" (grants carry how they were made; a sign-in's automatic grant never replaces a credential and is memory-only; OD-5-4's durable grants are the confirmations, reloaded as before). A reset KEEPS the key (rotating it would hand a stolen key's user the only key at once; kept, the owner can reset back -- a race, recorded).
w3l_account_policy_followup.credential_fence: The recovery selector stays ESCROW-3A's credential epoch for wallet tickets and grants (unchanged: a financial-protocol line). The password's generation is its scrypt hash (a fresh salt every time): every replacement carries the new store precondition `profile-password` (CAS on the hash; memory / file / journal / DynamoDB, merged into the profile Put) plus `profile-selector`; the KDF runs outside the identity queue and everything is re-checked inside it. A journaled `password-replaced` security event (journal first) lets an identity restore follow the hash chain and never re-install a retired password.
